title: Large Field-Free Superconducting Diode Effect with Nonmonotonic Polarity Reversals in NbSe$_2$/CrBr$_3$ Heterostructures
authors: Shengbiao Sun, Lang Xiao, Chenghao Shen, Bowen Hao, Jia-Peng Peng, Ziye Zhu, Feiyue Wang, Qilin Han, Ya-Qing Bie, Shuo Wang, Tong Zhou, Dapeng Yu, Ben-Chuan Lin
abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE), characterized by nonreciprocal dissipationless supercurrent, offers a promising route toward ultralow-power superconducting electronics. Yet most realizations require an external magnetic field, and achieving a large, controllable SDE at zero field remains challenging. Here we report a field-free SDE with an efficiency reaching 35.7% in a van der Waals NbSe$_2$/CrBr$_3$ heterostructure, whose polarity is programmable by magnetic-field history. Unlike conventional mechanisms based on finite-momentum pairing, the SDE originates from the leading symmetry-allowed cubic term odd in Cooper-pair momentum, which yields unequal critical currents while leaving the equilibrium condensate at zero momentum. Remarkably, upon sweeping a perpendicular magnetic field, the diode polarity undergoes nonmonotonic and hysteretic reversals that cannot be explained by Meissner screening or conventional ferromagnetic proximity. Combining transport measurements, micromagnetic simulations, and a generalized Ginzbur-Landau theory, we attribute these unconventional behaviors to layered ferrimagnetism in CrBr$_3$, where coexisting ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interlayer couplings produce a history-dependent interfacial exchange field acting on NbSe$_2$. Our results reveal a distinct mechanism for nonreciprocal superconductivity and establish layered van der Waals magnetism as a versatile platform for high-efficiency, programmable, field-free superconducting diodes.
summary: This paper reports a breakthrough in superconducting electronics by achieving a large, programmable superconducting diode effect (SDE) without an external magnetic field. The effect is realized in a $	ext{NbSe}_2/	ext{CrBr}_3$ heterostructure, where the nonreciprocity stems from a unique cubic momentum term coupled to the layered ferrimagnetism of $	ext{CrBr}_3$. This establishes a versatile platform for developing high-efficiency, memory-controlled superconducting devices.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is achieving a large, controllable superconducting diode effect (SDE) at zero external magnetic field, as most existing realizations require an external field.
main_result: The authors report a field-free SDE with a high efficiency (35.7%) in a vdW $	ext{NbSe}_2/	ext{CrBr}_3$ heterostructure, demonstrating that the diode polarity is programmable by the magnetic field history.
method: The study combines transport measurements, micromagnetic simulations, and a generalized Ginzburg-Landau theory to analyze the nonreciprocal supercurrent.
model_or_system: The system is a van der Waals heterostructure composed of the superconductor $	ext{NbSe}_2$ interfaced with the layered magnetic insulator $	ext{CrBr}_3$. The nonreciprocity is theoretically linked to a symmetry-allowed cubic term odd in the Cooper-pair momentum.
key_observables: Superconducting diode efficiency ($\eta$), nonreciprocal critical currents ($	ext{I}_{c+}$ vs $	ext{I}_{c-}$), and the hysteretic/nonmonotonic reversal of the diode polarity upon magnetic field sweeping.
important_parameters: The efficiency reached (35.7%), the specific material combination ($	ext{NbSe}_2/	ext{CrBr}_3$), and the dependence on the magnetic field history.
main_assumptions: The SDE mechanism is attributed to the layered ferrimagnetism in $	ext{CrBr}_3$ creating a history-dependent interfacial exchange field, distinguishing it from conventional mechanisms like Meissner screening.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the field-free SDE confirmation via differential resistance curves, map the efficiency ($\eta$) dependence on magnetic field showing hysteresis, and detail the theoretical link between the proximity field and the observed polarity reversals.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem (field-free SDE), presents the physical platform ($	ext{NbSe}_2/	ext{CrBr}_3$), develops the theoretical mechanism (cubic momentum term driven by layered ferrimagnetism), and validates the findings through comprehensive transport measurements and simulations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it demonstrates a mechanism for controlling non-equilibrium superconducting currents using magnetic memory effects in 2D heterostructures, which is a key area for advanced quantum electronics.
